UnitCommitOut.description: Everything the commit touched, as rows (architecture §4.1): the client patches what comes back.
UnitCommitOut.title: UnitCommitOut

UnitCounterLegIn.description:
The counter-leg a draft creates (spec §5.7). `temp_id` is the client's NEGATIVE id for the entry it
creates (preview rows carry it; a commit's `created` maps it to the real one). `received_amount` is the
amount received, an unsigned magnitude in minor units of the counter-account's currency (greater than
zero); the leg fixes the sign. It is required where the leg's offer says `needs_received_amount`
(problem `received_amount_required`) and refused otherwise (`received_amount_not_needed`).
UnitCounterLegIn.title: UnitCounterLegIn

UnitCounterLegOut.description: The counter-leg a commit would create on the offer's account (an unsynced one).
UnitCounterLegOut.title: UnitCounterLegOut

UnitDocumentDraftIn.description:
What the draft says of the transaction's document (spec §5.8, §6), on its ORIGINAL entry (any other
entry: 422 `invalid_draft`, `document_not_original`). `keep` (also: absent) leaves the link as it stands;
a commit that carries no document key for a transaction that is offered documents or awaits one is
refused, `document_decision_required`, unless the draft picks or says `none`. `pick` names a stored
`document_id` and the `document_version` the client saw (both required; a document another entry carries,
one that is gone or one at another version is a problem of the preview, and a conflict of a commit).
`none` decides that there is no document. `reresolve` drops the decision and the link: matching decides
afresh. `split_along_lines` picks `document_id` too and splits the transaction along its lines,
replacing an existing split (the entries it deletes are consequences of the preview). `decline_split`
keeps the split the preview proposes along the lines of a linked document from being made. A document
mode on a new entry, `document_id` or `document_version` on another mode, or `decline_split` on
`split_along_lines`, is 422 `invalid_draft` (`invalid_document`).

The split along the lines is draft state made of ordinary new entries. For a transaction that is stored
unsplit, has a linked or picked document of several lines with an exact total, and that the draft neither
splits nor declines, the preview adds one row per further line with a server-issued negative id and
`document_line`; the original entry takes the first line and the remainder. Once the client echoes any row
that carries a `document_line` (its id, `source_entry_id`, `amount`, `document_line` and its edits), the
split is the client's: nothing is regenerated and a row left out is removed. `split_along_lines` also
deletes the other stored entries of an existing split (consequences of kind `deleted`, with their
tags) and the client's own rows for the transaction. Anchor the draft on the original entry: the
anchor is never deleted.
UnitDocumentDraftIn.title: UnitDocumentDraftIn

UnitDocumentLineIn.description:
The line of a document a new entry was made from, as the preview showed it on the row
(`document_line`): echoed so an edit of a proposed row sticks to its line. A row whose document is no
longer the transaction's is dropped from the draft.
UnitDocumentLineIn.title: UnitDocumentLineIn

UnitDocumentSplitOut.description: The split along the lines of the document the transaction carries (a document of several lines).
UnitDocumentSplitOut.title: UnitDocumentSplitOut

UnitDocumentSummaryOut.description: A document in a few words: a suggestion, the one a transaction carries.
UnitDocumentSummaryOut.title: UnitDocumentSummaryOut

UnitDocumentWaitingOut.description:
The line of a transaction that waits for its document: "from <provider>, covered through <date>",
or "not synced yet" where `covered_through` is null.
UnitDocumentWaitingOut.title: UnitDocumentWaitingOut

UnitDraftEntryIn.description:
One entry the draft changes. `description` and `note` are left as stored when absent and emptied when
null. A new entry (negative `id`) names `source_entry_id`, a stored entry of the source it splits, and
carries its `amount`; the source's original entry is the residual and takes no amount of its own. `tags`
is a tag change on top of the stored (or inherited) tags; absent leaves them untouched.
UnitDraftEntryIn.title: UnitDraftEntryIn

UnitDraftIn.description:
The draft of the unit anchored on `anchor_entry_id`. `versions` map an entry id to the version the
client saw, for every entry of the unit (a commit carries them; a preview ignores them).
UnitDraftIn.title: UnitDraftIn

UnitFieldDraftIn.description:
`keep`: untouched (a commit accepts what resolution makes of it). `fixed`: the user's `value` (null
leaves the field empty). `reresolve`: the passes decide this field again.
UnitFieldDraftIn.title: UnitFieldDraftIn

UnitFieldOut.description: One derived field of a row as the draft leaves it.
UnitFieldOut.title: UnitFieldOut

UnitKeyOut.description: A derivation key: the pass and its basis (a `user` key's basis is the proposal it accepted).
UnitKeyOut.title: UnitKeyOut

UnitOfferEffectOut.description: What picking the offer would also do (the real consequences show after the pick).
UnitOfferEffectOut.title: UnitOfferEffectOut

UnitOfferOut.description:
A partner a transfer leg may be given. The groups come in this order: open offers (`open_leg`,
`untyped_entry`), legs paired elsewhere, the counter-leg; within the first two, exact amounts first,
then by date distance (earlier `booked_on`, then lower id on a tie).
UnitOfferOut.title: UnitOfferOut

UnitPairingIn.description:
What the draft says of a transfer leg's partner (spec §5.7). `keep` (also: absent) leaves it, and a
commit accepts the proposal the preview shows. `pick` names a stored partner entry (`partner_entry_id`,
positive): it must be an offer of the leg, else the preview lists the problem `partner_not_offered` or
`partner_in_unit`. `counter_leg` (with `counter_leg`) creates the other side on the leg's unsynced
counter-account: refused with `counter_leg_not_offered` for a leg that has a partner or no usable
counter-account, `counter_leg_account_synced` for a synced one. `reresolve` drops the stored pair and
lets the passes decide again. A `pairing` on an entry that is not a transfer leg, a negative partner id,
or a `counter_leg` object on another mode, is 422 `invalid_draft`.
UnitPairingIn.title: UnitPairingIn

UnitPartnerOut.description: A leg in a few words: the partner of a leg, or the one a leg paired elsewhere is paired with.
UnitPartnerOut.title: UnitPartnerOut

UnitPreviewOut.description: What committing the draft would do. Nothing was written.
UnitPreviewOut.title: UnitPreviewOut

UnitProblemOut.description: A way the result would break an invariant (a commit is refused for it): a code, never prose.
UnitProblemOut.title: UnitProblemOut

UnitRowDocumentLineOut.description: The line a row has (spec §5.8), with its description; a row made from a line echoes it back.
UnitRowDocumentLineOut.title: UnitRowDocumentLineOut

UnitRowDocumentOut.description:
The document part of a transaction's original entry (spec §5.8, §6). Null where there is nothing to
say: no link, no key, no suggestion, no wait. A suggestion is no decision: where `decision_required`, a
commit is refused (`document_decision_required`) unless it picks one or says `none`.
UnitRowDocumentOut.title: UnitRowDocumentOut

UnitShownBasisIn.description: The key of the proposal the client showed for a value (`pass` is history, llm or matcher_proposal).
UnitShownBasisIn.title: UnitShownBasisIn

UnitSplitOut.description: One source transaction's allocation: the residual is its original entry.
UnitSplitOut.title: UnitSplitOut

UnitSuggestedSplitOut.description:
How a `pair_unequal` is fixed: a new flow entry of `amount` (signed like the larger leg) split off the
larger leg's source, named by one of its stored entries (`source_entry_id`).
UnitSuggestedSplitOut.title: UnitSuggestedSplitOut

UnitTagChangeIn.description:
A change of an entry's tags relative to its stored tags (a new entry's: the original's). A tag in both
lists is 422 `invalid_draft` (`tag_conflict`); duplicates are tolerated.
UnitTagChangeIn.title: UnitTagChangeIn

UnitTransferOut.description: A transfer leg as the draft leaves it (spec §5.7): its state, partner and offers, computed now.
UnitTransferOut.title: UnitTransferOut

UpdateBody.description:
Absent fields stay; `null` clears `external_ref`, `note`, `icon` and `color`.

No currency, no kind: they never change.
UpdateBody.title: UpdateBody

post.description:
Write the draft in one transaction, then settle. A commit does not confirm: settling does.

409 `conflict` names the entries whose version moved (or that `versions` omitted); 409 `unit_moved` is a
closure that changed under the locks, or a picked document that another entry carries (`details.reason`
`taken`) or that is at another version (`version`), named in `details.document_id`; 409
`stale_reference` a category, payee, account or picked document that no longer exists; 409 `try_again`
a deadlock lost twice. 422 carries the code of the first problem the preview would
list (all of them in `details.problems`), or `invalid_draft`. A pick is checked against the widest window
(90 days), so one the widened preview accepted commits. `window_days` (1 to 90, default the matching
window) is the window the proposals were shown for: send the one the preview used, so the proposals a
commit accepts (as the user's decisions) are the ones shown.

401.description: Not signed in (or wrong login or password).

post.description:
The unit as a commit of the draft would leave it, resolved fresh: rows, keys, flags, the state it leads
to, the problems that would refuse the commit and the consequences. An in-memory overlay: nothing is
written.

Settling is simulated ledger-wide: a leg of the unit that settling would pair with a leg outside it brings
that leg's unit into the rows. Each transfer row carries `transfer`: its state, partner and offers.
`window_days` (1 to 90, default the matching window) is the window the offers are shown for.
